relationships.subject: small fiber neuropathy
relationships.evidence_quote: The evidence strongly supports SFN as a key factor in the pathophysiology of BMS, particularly due to reductions in nerve fiber density and altered sensory thresholds.

relationships.subject: burning mouth syndrome
relationships.evidence_quote: Additionally, an increase in TRPV1-positive, NGF-positive, and P2X3-positive fibers, overexpression of Nav1.7, and slight underexpression of Nav1.9 mRNA were observed in BMS patients.

key_findings: Systematic review of 20 studies: reduced intraepithelial nerve fiber density (30-60%) and altered thermal thresholds in BMS support small fiber neuropathy.
BMS tongue shows increased TRPV1, NGF and P2X3 positive fibers; Nav1.7 findings were inconsistent across studies.
